description: The 35,842 t gap is not a typo. The 2008-09 yearbook prints floodplain 879,513 t. The 2016-17 yearbook (Table 3.40) retroactively splits this into floodplain 843,671 t + seasonal cultured waterbody 35,842 t. The 2024-25 yearbook kept the split floodplain figure but left the 2008-09 seasonal cultured waterbody cell empty.
impact: The 2024-25 back table under-counts 2008-09 culture by 35,842 t.
handling: Use 2016-17 Table 3.40 for 2008-09 (floodplain 843,671; SCWB 35,842).

description: The 2 t gap in the 2024-25 back table comes from Live fish (152,241 vs 152,242 t) and Exotic carp (476,761 vs 476,762 t). The 2018-19 yearbook's own Table 3.2 adds up exactly.
impact: Negligible.
handling: Use the 2018-19 yearbook values.

impact: Negligible
handling: Choose one table as the primary source per variable and record which.

description: 2002-03 'Flood Land' (capture) INCLUDED semi-closed seasonal waterbodies. Later yearbooks report them as 'Seasonal Cultured Waterbody' under CULTURE.
impact: Capture vs culture shares are not comparable across the break; capture share is overstated in early years.
handling: Use the harmonized 'Floodplain complex' (floodplain + SCWB + pen) for long-run series.

description: SCWB appears in 2009-10 (46,902 t). In 2011-12 floodplain falls by 100,897 t while SCWB rises by 80,933 t.
impact: Spurious decline in floodplain capture.
handling: Same as ISSUE-04; consider a break dummy in models.

description: Pangas split out from Catfish and Tilapia from Other Inland Fish in 2013-14. In that year Other Catfish falls from 360,722 to 81,536 t and Other Inland Fish from 835,457 to 524,488 t.
impact: Group series break unless re-aggregated.
handling: Harmonize to 'Catfish (incl. pangas)' and 'Other inland fish (incl. tilapia...)'.

description: River catch jumps +93,181 t (+52%), and hilsa jumps +101,466 t in the same year.
impact: Likely a change in hilsa estimation, not a real 52% rise.
handling: Read the 2016-17 yearbook methodology chapter; add a break dummy.

description: Marine industrial jumps from 41,665 to 73,386 t (+76%).
impact: Possible change in coverage or reporting of trawlers.
handling: Check the 2011-12 yearbook.

description: Marine artisanal -12.1% (513,819 to 451,661 t) while marine shrimp +97% (26,269 to 51,740 t). The yearbook message says marine statistics were updated with support from the SCMF Project and the MFSMU.
impact: The 2024-25 marine numbers may not be comparable with earlier years.
handling: Treat as a possible break; check for a methodology note.

description: Beel 114,161 ha and Kaptai 68,800 ha are identical in 2002-03 and 2024-25. River/beel areas come from the 1981-83 frame survey / SPARRSO 1983.
impact: Capture productivity (kg/ha) is not independently measured.
handling: Do not interpret capture kg/ha trends as ecological change.

description: 2002-03 river area 1,031,563 ha included the Sundarbans; 2024-25 shows 853,863 + 177,700 = 1,031,563 ha.
impact: Area is consistent once added back.
handling: Harmonize via xwalk_sector.

description: 2002-03 assigns all Sundarbans catch to Khulna; 2024-25 splits it across Bagerhat (27,369), Khulna (1,376) and Satkhira (1,400).
impact: District-level comparisons for these three districts are distorted.
handling: Exclude Sundarbans from district comparisons, or analyse the three districts together.

description: Kaptai Lake: 'Others' 10.7% of catch in 2002-03 (Kachki, Chapila, Kazoli, Bacha shown separately) vs 'Other Fish' 96.2% in 2024-25. Beel: Punti, Tengra, Baim, Chapila, Pabda, Chital/Phali listed separately in 2002-03 and lumped together in 2024-25.
impact: Species-level diversity indices cannot be computed consistently from the yearbooks for small indigenous species.
handling: Use group-level indicators; get species data from BFDC Kaptai landing records or FRSS raw CAS data.

description: Other Carp: Kalia (2002-03) became Bata (2024-25). Catfish: Bacha in 2002-03, absent in 2024-25. Exotic carp now adds Bighead and Black carp.
impact: Small composition effects inside groups.
handling: Document in xwalk_species; sensitivity check.

description: Crab included from 2015-16. Cuchia reported from 2019-20 (unclear whether newly covered or split from 'Other inland fish').
impact: Adds to totals without a matching earlier value.
handling: Exclude crab from like-for-like totals; flag cuchia.

description: Sardine reported from 2011-12 and Tuna from 2020-21, presumably from 'Other marine fish'.
impact: Break in Other marine fish.
handling: Harmonize into 'Other marine fish (incl. sardine, tuna)'.

description: Pangas is listed as Pangasius pangasius (native). Cultured pangas in Bangladesh is widely reported to be mainly P. hypophthalmus (exotic Thai pangas).
impact: Affects any native vs exotic classification.
handling: Confirm with DoF/FRSS before classifying pangas as native.

description: 13 district spellings changed (e.g., Jessore to Jashore, Comilla to Cumilla, Nawabganj to Chapai Nawabganj). Khagrachhari has no data row in 2002-03. Rangpur (2010) and Mymensingh (2015) divisions did not exist in 2002-03.
impact: Joins fail without a crosswalk.
handling: Use xwalk_district (2025 divisions applied to all years).

description: Values for overlapping years printed in different yearbooks are identical, except where noted (I27, I39, I40, I41).
impact: No retroactive revision of the back series was detected.
handling: Back-series tables in recent yearbooks can fill gaps.

description: The 2024-25 PDF is a 96 dpi scan with no text layer. Values were read visually and verified against printed row/column totals. Scanned copies were also used for 2004-05, 2008-09, 2020-21, 2021-22 and 2022-23.
impact: Transcription risk where no total exists.
handling: Prefer DoF website PDFs with a text layer; double-entry for tables without totals.

description: Cox's Bazar is the only district whose inland total fell (45,007 to 38,164 t). Pond output fell from 17,726 to 6,132 t while national pond output rose 3.3x.
impact: Could be real (land use change) or a reporting change.
handling: Check the intermediate yearbooks for when the drop occurs.

description: Floodplain catch rises 25% (497,922 to 621,443 t) while pond output falls 5% (795,810 to 756,993 t); culture total falls. The yearbook note says: 'Pond production is decreased and open water catch is increased due to flood.' Floodplain keeps rising afterwards (718,491 t in 2005-06; 768,830 t in 2006-07), so the level shift persists beyond the flood year.
impact: Capture share jumps from 35% to 39-41%; long-run capture/culture trends have a break here as well as at 2009-10.
handling: Flag 2004-05 onwards; consider break dummies at 2004-05 and 2009-10.

description: The 2006-07 note says Major Carp = Rui, Catla, Mrigal, Kalbasu and Other Carp = Ghania only. But the data still put Kalbasu in Other Carp (Kaptai 'Other Carp' 179 t = Kalbasu 169 + Gonia 10 in Table 11), as in 2005-06 (122 = 121 + 1).
impact: Group definition appears unchanged in practice; the note is likely a wording error.
handling: Keep 2006-07 groups as comparable with earlier years; mention in notes.

description: Sundarbans catch is split across Bagerhat, Khulna and Satkhira from at least 2004-05 (2004-05: 12,925 / 1,675 / 1,124 t). In 2002-03 it was all assigned to Khulna.
impact: Updates I12: the change happened between 2002-03 and 2004-05.
handling: Check the 2003-04 yearbook for the exact year.

description: Shrimp-farm figures are printed with decimals; division and grand totals differ from the sum of district totals by 2-3 t (Dhaka division).
impact: Negligible.
handling: Keep printed values.

description: Shrimp farm area 141,353 ha (2002-03) becomes 217,877 ha from 2004-05; pond area 290,500 ha becomes 305,025 ha.
impact: Per-hectare productivity of shrimp farms is not comparable across the change.
handling: Note in Table 3 of Volume 1.

description: The 2016-17 yearbook moves part of the original 'Flood Land' (capture) into 'Seasonal cultured waterbody' (culture) for 2005-06 to 2008-09: 27,738 / 30,157 / 32,931 / 35,842 t. The original yearbooks reported the whole amount as floodplain capture. Years up to 2004-05 were not revised.
impact: Two versions of the capture/culture split exist for 2005-06 to 2008-09; national totals are identical in both.
handling: Volume 1: use the revised (2016-17) split from 2005-06 onward and say so in a note; Volume 2: keep both versions.

description: The district table fails its own checks. The beel column repeats the division total for every district in Mymensingh (18,629) and Khulna (5,405) divisions; 62 of 64 district rows do not add up to their printed totals (e.g. Dhaka parts 20,714 vs total 20,721); district totals sum to 3,606,804 t vs the printed national 3,496,958 t.
impact: 2016-17 district figures cannot be verified; beel values for 14 districts are wrong.
handling: Volume 2: keep as printed with a strong flag. Volume 1: do not use 2016-17 district data; prefer a later yearbook's figure if one is printed.

description: Table 3.1 note 1: 'River & Estuary production has been increased due to high growth of Hilsa production.' Hilsa rose from 394,951 t (2015-16) to 496,417 t (2016-17).
impact: Confirms the river jump is driven by hilsa estimates.
handling: Keep I07 flag; quote the yearbook's explanation in the note.

description: 'Other carp' jumps from 11,155 t (2008-09) to 64,359 t (2009-10), and Major carp/Other inland fish/Shrimp also shift. 2006-07 to 2008-09 notes put Kalbasu in Major carp; later notes put Kalibaus and Bata in Other carp.
impact: Carp group series not comparable across 2008-09/2009-10.
handling: Use a combined 'all native carps' (Major + Other carp) series for long-run comparisons.

description: River area shown as 853,863 ha and Sundarbans as 177,700 ha from 2007-08 (previously 1,031,563 ha combined). Floodplain area 2,832,792 ha until 2008-09, then 2,712,618 ha by 2016-17 (pen culture and seasonal culture areas carved out).
impact: Per-hectare figures change partly because areas are redefined.
handling: Note in area table.

description: Beel mirror/common carp is 2,455 t in Table 3.3 but 2,453 t in Table 3.13 (beel column of Table 3.3 sums to 98,119 vs 98,117).
impact: Negligible.
handling: Use Table 3.13 for beel species detail.

description: Kaptai Lake species table switches to the grouped format: 'Other fish' = 93.5% (Chapila, Kachki, Kazoli, Bacha etc. no longer shown separately). In 2008-09 they were still listed separately.
impact: Updates I13: species detail for Kaptai is lost between 2008-09 and 2016-17.
handling: Check 2009-10..2015-16 yearbooks to find the year of change.

description: In the species x waterbody table, the beel cell for big shrimp/prawn is blank (0), but the row total (121,203 t) and Table 12 (Golda 489 t) include 489 t. The beel column therefore sums to 81,075 t instead of 81,564 t.
impact: Beel big shrimp under-counted by 489 t in that table only.
handling: Keep as printed; flag. Use Table 12 for beel species detail.

description: 'Semi closed (Flood Plain)' appears as a separate culture item for the first time (46,902 t, 22,382 ha). Floodplain area changes from 2,832,792 ha to 2,810,410 ha.
impact: Confirms I05: the capture/culture break starts in 2009-10 in the original yearbooks.
handling: Floodplain complex harmonization as before.

description: The 2010-11 yearbook still prints the unsplit floodplain for 2005-06 to 2008-09 (e.g. 879,513 t for 2008-09). The retroactive split (I27) appears later (seen in 2016-17).
impact: Narrows when the revision was made.
handling: Check 2011-12 to 2015-16 yearbooks for the first appearance.

description: 2009-10 note: Other Carp = Ghania, Kalbasu. 2010-11 note: Other Carp = Ghania, Kalibaus, Bata; Cat Fish = Boal, Air, Pangas, Silon, Rita (Bacha dropped); Exotic carp adds Big Head. 2006-07 to 2008-09 notes put Kalbasu in Major Carp.
impact: Explains the jump in 'Other carp' from 11,155 t (2008-09) to 64,359 t (2009-10).
handling: Use 'all native carps' combined series for long-run comparisons.

description: Rangpur division appears in the district table for the first time (7 divisions).
impact: None for district data; affects division subtotals.
handling: Use 2025 divisions for all years.

where: YFSB 2012-13 Table 35 vs YFSB 2016-17 Table 3.40 and YFSB 2024-25 Table 3.45
description: The 2012-13 yearbook retroactively splits floodplain into floodplain + seasonal cultured waterbody back to 2002-03 (2002-03: 414,823 + 60,293; 2003-04: 437,509 + 60,413; 2004-05: 554,762 + 66,681). Later yearbooks only keep the split from 2005-06 (2016-17 Table 3.40 starts 2005-06; 2024-25 Table 3.45 shows 2003-04 unsplit, 497,922).
impact: Three different capture/culture splits exist for 2002-03 to 2004-05 depending on the yearbook used.
handling: Volume 1: state which version is used. Prefer the latest yearbook that covers the year; mention the alternative.

where: FSYB 2011-12 Table 1 vs YFSB 2012-13 Table 35 and later
description: 2011-12 pond 1,342,282 t and seasonal cultured waterbody 182,293 t in its own yearbook; revised to 1,392,412 and 132,163 t from the 2012-13 yearbook on (50,130 t moved from seasonal culture to pond; same total).
impact: Pond vs seasonal culture split for 2011-12 depends on the source.
handling: Use the revised figures (later yearbooks) for the national series; keep originals in Volume 2.

description: Species groups for 2012-13 differ between Table 2 (e.g. Major carp 729,362; Shrimp 231,842) and Table 36 of the same yearbook (731,662; 228,769). Later yearbooks use the Table 36 figures. Totals are identical.
impact: Small differences in species-group series for 2012-13.
handling: Use Table 36 / later yearbooks for the national species series; Table 2 kept in Volume 2.

description: Kaptai Lake species table switches to the grouped format in 2011-12: 'Other fish' 84-88% of catch. 2010-11 still listed Chapila (2,727 t), Kachki (2,558 t), Mola (480 t), Kazoli, Bacha separately.
impact: Species-level series for Kaptai small pelagic fish ends in 2010-11.
handling: Updates I13/I33.

description: From 2011-12 beel production is split into 'Natural source' and 'Beel nursery' (stocked fish): 2011-12: 60,887 + 24,321 t; 2012-13: 77,837 + 10,065 t. Beel is reported as capture although part of it is stocked.
impact: Beel 'capture' includes stocking; wild-catch interpretation is overstated.
handling: Note in Volume 1; keep the split in Volume 2 where printed.

description: The Barisal division subtotal row is partly missing in the PDF text layer; all district rows and the national total reconcile.
impact: None (division subtotals are recomputed).
handling: No action.

description: Sector-wise national production for 1984-85 to 1992-93 is available from the 2012-13 yearbook's 30-year table. Overlapping years (1983-84, 1993-94 to 2001-02) are identical to other yearbooks.
impact: National sector series can be extended to 1983-84 to 2024-25 without gaps.
handling: Use for Volume 1 Table 1/2.

description: The district table does not reconcile: about 30 districts' printed totals differ from the sum of their parts (e.g. Jashore parts 222,675 t vs printed total 250,757 t; Khulna parts exceed total by 7,000 t); division river subtotals sum to 318,456 t vs printed national river 320,598 t. Column sums of districts otherwise match the national totals. The PDF text layer is also corrupted (digits split across lines), so values were read from page images.
impact: 2017-18 district totals are unreliable; component columns are usable with caution.
handling: Volume 2: keep as printed with flag; Volume 1: show district figures only from years that reconcile, or note the problem.

description: Tilapia is 381,215 t in Table 3.2 but 384,737 t in Table 3.3; Other inland fish 554,558 t vs 551,036 t (3,522 t difference = cage culture tilapia). Table 3.2 inland column sums to 1 t less than its printed total.
impact: Small inconsistency between national species table and species x waterbody table.
handling: Use Table 3.2 (consistent with later yearbooks) for the national species series.

description: Sector and species figures in the 2014-15 and 2017-18 yearbooks are identical to the back series printed in the 2024-25 yearbook; 2017-18 Table 3.40 is identical to 2016-17 Table 3.40 for 2005-06 to 2016-17.
impact: Confirms stability of the national series from 2005-06 onward.
handling: None.

description: The PDF text layer truncates some decimals (e.g. '4.' for a shrimp-farm value) and wraps Jessore's shrimp-farm value (35,574 t) to a separate line. Values were taken by position from the PDF; all district rows add up, national totals differ by under 70 t (rounding in source).
impact: None after correction.
handling: No action.

description: District tables of 2015-16, 2018-19 and 2019-20 reconcile at district, division and national level, unlike 2016-17 and 2017-18 (I28, I46).
impact: District data available and reliable for these years.
handling: None.

description: Cuchia appears as a separate group (13,424 t) and the note also lists Cuchia under Live fish. Live fish and Cuchia are listed separately and both add into the total (no double counting). Cuchia in Table 3.3 is 13,425 t (1 t rounding).
impact: Group definitions: Cuchia was probably inside 'Other inland fish' or 'Live fish' before 2019-20.
handling: Updates I15; keep Cuchia as a separate (new) group.

description: 'Crab production has included from this year' (13,160 t; area 19,408 ha, included in shrimp farm area).
impact: Confirms crab is new coverage from 2015-16.
handling: As I15.

description: The supplied scan of the 2021-22 yearbook has no Tables 3.1-3.3 (it goes from methodology text to Table 3.4). Sector figures were taken from the Key Findings table of the same book (identical to YFSB 2024-25 Table 3.43); species groups from YFSB 2024-25 Table 3.44 with the inland/marine split for hilsa and shrimp from Key Findings (inland totals reconcile exactly).
impact: No species x waterbody table for 2021-22.
handling: Note in Volume 2 sources; obtain a complete copy for a later version.

description: The 2022-23 scan is 72 dpi. Noakhali river catch read as 15,153 t (could be read as 15,133); 15,153 is the only value consistent with the row, division and national totals.
impact: None after reconciliation.
handling: None.

description: Crab is printed as an indented sub-line ('-Crab*', 10,782 t) under Shrimp/Prawn farm, but it is additional to the shrimp-farm figure: the country total includes it. Same layout in 2020-21 and 2022-23.
impact: Easy to miss crab when transcribing; totals 10-13 thousand t short otherwise.
handling: Crab kept as a separate sector row.

description: All four years: national sector and species figures identical to YFSB 2024-25 back tables; all district tables reconcile at district, division and national level.
impact: Reliable.
handling: None.
